summary: Akira Omine was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University and Heidelberg University. His career included posts at Kyoto University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University, and Ryukoku University.

A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, Akira Sadakata studied under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, completing studies at the University of Tokyo and the University of Paris. He held faculty posts at Tokai University from around 1971 to 2007.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Akira Saitō studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikidō Takasaki and at the Australian National University. He held positions at Mie University, the University of Tokyo, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Akira Shimada works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and Daud Ali, and has held posts at the British Museum and the State University of New York at New Paltz.

Akira Suganuma was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University. He later held academic positions at Toyo University from around 1962 to 1994 and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies in 1981.
Akira Unete works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He has been affiliated with Otani University, attested as an associate professor in 2010, and with the Otani Academic Society, attested in 2026.

Akira Yuyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji, Akira Hirakawa, Jan Willem de Jong, and Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at the Australian National University, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Soka University.

Akitoshi Saito was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held posts at Taisho University, attested between 1982 and 2014, and served as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies, attested in 2014.
Akong Tulku Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1967, he founded Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre, where he later served as abbot.
Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran works in Indology and philosophy. A doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago, Parmeswaran is attested as a researcher at Ghent University in 2026.
Akshay Ramanlal Desai was a scholar in history and archaeology. Between 1937 and 1946, he studied at the University of Mumbai, where he was a student under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye.
Alan Entwistle was an Indologist who completed his studies at the University of Southampton between 1968 and 1971 and at SOAS University of London between 1971 and 1982.

Alan Fox is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and sinology who earned his PhD from Temple University. He has held faculty appointments in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Delaware.

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He received his PhD from Harvard University, where he was supervised by Parimal G. Patil and taught by Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans was an art and architectural historian who studied at the University of Toronto in 1946 and at Princeton University in 1948 and 1950.

Alan John Bayard Wace was an archaeologist who studied at Pembroke College under Robert Alexander Neil. His career included posts at the British School at Athens, the Victoria and Albert Museum, the University of Cambridge, and Alexandria University.
Alan Lomax pursued his education at Choate Rosemary Hall, St. Mark's School of Texas, the University of Texas at Austin, Harvard University, and Columbia University.
Alan Nussbaum is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Harvard University between 1969 and 1976. He held a post at Cornell University around 1985.

Alan Sponberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia. He held faculty posts at Princeton University during the 1980s and at Stanford University in 1988.

Alan Watts was a scholar and writer in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Dimitrije Mitrinović, Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, and Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki. He held positions at Northwestern University, the American Academy of Asian Studies, and the Esalen Institute.
